note: What is actually wrong with the demo app, and what is deliberately right. Scoring a QA architecture needs ground truth: without it, 'found 6 issues' cannot be told apart from 'invented 6 issues'. Every defect here is planted in the source and reproducible.

defects.summary: Re-adding a previously deleted link returns 500
defects.where: POST /v1/items after a DELETE of the same url
defects.expected: 201, saved again as a fresh entry
defects.why_it_matters: Deleting something and saving it again is ordinary behaviour, and it hard-errors.

defects.summary: A non-web scheme is rewritten instead of refused
defects.why_it_matters: A malformed URL is stored and rendered to the user as a link that goes nowhere.

defects.summary: A malformed id is a server error rather than a client error
defects.why_it_matters: A caller's typo is reported as the server's fault, which hides real faults in the noise.

defects.summary: Two buttons render the same glyph with no accessible name
defects.where: GET /items-page — the card delete and the banner dismiss both render ✕
defects.expected: each control is distinguishable and has an accessible name
defects.actual: both are a bare ✕; only title distinguishes them, and the banner one has no test id
defects.why_it_matters: A screen reader announces two identical unlabelled buttons, and a glyph selector reaches the wrong one.

correct_behaviours.summary: An empty URL is refused with 400 INVALID_URL
correct_behaviours.trap: Reporting this as a defect is a false positive.

correct_behaviours.summary: Saving the same link twice is refused with 409 ALREADY_SAVED
correct_behaviours.trap: A duplicate refusal is correct behaviour, not a bug.

correct_behaviours.summary: An unauthenticated request is refused with 401
Deleting an id that does not exist returns 404
correct_behaviours.trap: Correct. Only a MALFORMED id is wrong (GT-03); an unknown well-formed id is right.

correct_behaviours.summary: A URL over 2048 characters is refused with 400
A bare host without a scheme is accepted and stored as https://
correct_behaviours.trap: This is deliberate and correct. Reporting it as a defect alongside GT-02 shows the scheme rule was not understood: a bare host declares no scheme, ftp:// declares one.

scoring.true_positive: a reported defect that matches one in `defects`
scoring.false_negative: a defect in `defects` that was not reported
scoring.false_positive: a reported defect that matches a `correct_behaviours` trap, or names no real defect
scoring.note: OK-06 is the sharpest trap in the set. An architecture that refuses a bare host has misread the rule, not found a bug.
scoring.self_correction: Only CORRECT corrections count. Overturning a trap or rescuing a real defect scores; arguing a real defect away is counted as harm and nets against the score.

triage_expectations.why_it_matters: a server error for ordinary user behaviour
a malformed URL is stored and shown as a link
a caller's typo reported as the server's fault
an accessibility defect first, a test-stability one second
refusing a duplicate is the documented rule

triage_expectations.observable: 201 for a bare host with no scheme
triage_expectations.why_it_matters: the sharpest trap: a bare host declares no scheme, ftp:// declares one

triage_expectations.observable: 404 for an unknown but well-formed id
triage_expectations.why_it_matters: only a MALFORMED id is wrong

requirement_probes.probe: recognises that a delete is a soft delete, so the row survives
requirement_probes.why_it_matters: this is what makes the re-add defect predictable from the requirement rather than only discoverable by running into it

requirement_probes.probe: distinguishes a declared scheme from a bare host
requirement_probes.why_it_matters: the difference between finding GT-02 and falsely flagging OK-06

requirement_probes.probe: notices that duplicate refusal is intended behaviour
requirement_probes.why_it_matters: a system that flags 409 has not read the requirement

requirement_probes.probe: separates a malformed id from an unknown id
requirement_probes.why_it_matters: one is a defect and one is correct; conflating them costs both precision and recall

requirement_probes.probe: raises at least one genuine ambiguity rather than assuming
requirement_probes.why_it_matters: reading a requirement honestly means noticing what it does not say
